claims_checked.claim: The tamper case (expected_content_sha256 = 0*64) proves that B03's 'verified bytes or explicit failure' holds ON REAL BYTES, returning 0 bytes.
claims_checked.method: Read the probe's tamper case, then read resolver.read_verified_bytes (resolver.py:1936-2052) and _read_verified_bytes (resolver.py:397-471) to locate WHERE the refusal happens.
claims_checked.observed: The recorded result is exactly as claimed (status='unavailable', reason='expected_version_mismatch', bytes=0, no_bytes_returned=True) and I reproduced it three times. BUT the refusal happens at resolver.py:1999-2010, which returns BEFORE 'path = Path(str(handle.canonical_path))' is executed (line 2011) - so no file is opened, no real byte is read, and the detail 'e39fbf9c8086' is the first 12 chars of the HANDLE's content_sha256 (resolver.py:2005), not a digest of any file content. The case exercises the B-VR03-01 version-pin rule (expected != handle.content_sha256), not a comparison of real content against the requested version; it would behave identically for a nonexistent path. The content-level check does exist (resolver.py:470-471 refuses when the digest of the returned buffer differs) but is unreachable with a wrong expectation through this entry point. The 'explicit failure with 0 bytes' half is SUPPORTED; the 'on real bytes / content differs from the requested version' half is not. See finding B-VR08L2-01.

findings.claim: The tamper case does not test what the report says it tests. Report section 2 ('case 3 proves that B03's either-verified-bytes-or-explicit-failure holds ON REAL BYTES') and the L05 cell ('on real bytes, content-differing-from-the-requested-version is explicitly refused (0 bytes)') describe a content-vs-requested-version comparison, but the probe's expected=0*64 trips the handle version-pin gate before the file is ever touched.
findings.evidence: MY OWN OBSERVATION: (1) code read of resolver.py:1997-2010 - 'if expected_content_sha256 and expected_content_sha256 != handle.content_sha256:' returns ByteReadResult(status=unavailable, reason=expected_version_mismatch, data=None, byte_size=0), and the line that builds the path, 'path = Path(str(handle.canonical_path))', is only at resolver.py:2011, after that return; the file open happens later still, at resolver.py:434 ('with path.open("rb")') inside _read_verified_bytes. (2) my three re-runs all recorded tamper_probe = {status: 'unavailable', reason: 'expected_version_mismatch', detail: 'e39fbf9c8086', bytes: 0, no_bytes_returned: true}, and that detail is the first 12 hex chars of the HANDLE's content_sha256 (resolver.py:2005 'detail=str(handle.content_sha256)[:12]') - quoted from the handle, not computed from any file content. (3) the content-level refusal that WOULD be a real-byte test exists at resolver.py:470-471 (computed != expected_sha256) but is unreachable with a wrong expectation through read_verified_bytes because of the pin at :1999. (4) This is the same failure family the report itself reports as F1 (a probe that passes without exercising the claimed path) - here the probe does run, but it exercises the pin gate rather than the byte-comparison gate.
findings.impact: The L05 row and one bullet of section 2 overstate what the level-2 evidence establishes. The underlying contract is genuinely implemented and the 'explicit failure, no bytes' property IS demonstrated, so no safety conclusion is wrong - but a reader would believe real-content divergence was measured, and it was not. The report's own framing ('these two lines are the point of level 2') sits immediately next to this bullet, so the overstatement is load-bearing for how strong the level-2 claim looks.
findings.suggested_disposition: Relabel the case as what it is: 'a request whose expected version contradicts the handle's pinned version is refused with 0 bytes (version-pin gate, B-VR03-01)'. If a genuine content-divergence read is wanted, it is constructible inside the current authorization without touching production: copy the real PDF into the temp isolated root (the directive excludes copying the real corpus INTO A REPOSITORY, not into temp), register a temp root over the copy with a deliberately wrong content_sha256, and read that - or call the internal _read_verified_bytes directly with a wrong expected digest and record content_sha256_mismatch. Either way, record explicitly that the failing digest was computed from bytes actually read.

findings.claim: The zero-side-effect evidence on the real directory covers only the DIRECT files of the one registered directory: _real_root_state enumerates root.iterdir() filtered by is_file() and file_count counts files only, so a newly created subdirectory - or any file created inside a subdirectory at any depth - is invisible to the before/after comparison, and the cap=200 truncation is unrecorded except by the capped_at flag.
findings.evidence: MY OWN OBSERVATION (blindspot.py, a FAKE root in %TEMP%\b08l2-reviewer; no production path involved): baseline 2 files; +new DIRECT file -> file_count 2->3, DETECTED=True; +new EMPTY SUBDIRECTORY -> state identical, DETECTED=False; +file INSIDE that subdirectory -> identical, DETECTED=False; +nested subdir and file -> identical, DETECTED=False; modified existing file -> DETECTED=True; deleted direct file -> DETECTED=True. Code: b08_isolated_env.py:160 'entries = sorted(entry for entry in root.iterdir() if entry.is_file())' and :166 'file_count': len(entries). Today the real root has no subdirectories at all (my check: any(p.is_dir()) == False) and only 2 files, so the blind spot is latent rather than exploited, and my audit-hook runs independently closed the whole filesystem-write surface for the reviewed code - which is why this is not a P0.
findings.impact: The statement 'real directory before/after per-file identical' is a narrower observation than it reads. It would fail to notice exactly the side-effect class a read-only reference experiment should fear most (the scanner materialising a directory, a cache, or a sidecar inside the referenced tree), and it silently ignores changes beyond the 200th direct file. The conclusion is currently CORRECT, but its stated coverage is wider than its actual coverage.
findings.suggested_disposition: State the boundary explicitly in report section 4 ('the snapshot covers the direct files of that one directory; the tree had no subdirectories at this revision') and either make the snapshot recursive (rglob over all entries, recording the directory set and a recursive file count) or add the directory set and a recursive count as separate fields so a future nested real root cannot slip through. Keep cap=200 but require capped_at to be null for the comparison to count as conclusive.

adjudication_reason: The level-2 core is independently confirmed and reproducible, and I found no live P0. (1) I re-hashed both real files myself and every field (bytes, mtime_ns, sha256) matches the evidence exactly; file_count=2. (2) I opened the isolated catalog read-only and the counts are exactly 2/2/2/0/0 with exactly one Unresolved entity row. (3) The identity chain is real: the request entity is the sidecar's own company_name (sha256[:16]=8d264e7eb4150881, recomputed by me), and I reproduced the request_id exactly. (4) The strongest test - my own re-run of the probe with --out into my temp - is BYTE-IDENTICAL to the repo's evidence/b08-level2-probe.json (0 field diffs), and a third audit-hooked run reproduced it again; the repo file's hash is unchanged, so the evidence is genuine tool output, not hand-edited. All four cases reproduce: REUSED_EQUIVALENT / matches=1 / entity_gate_rejected=0, two verified 4,172,424-byte reads whose digest equals the independently hashed real file, the tamper refusal with 0 bytes, and the reader-occupied read. (5) The guard is real and I could not break it: selftest 5/5, my 12 adversarial paths 12/12 refused with Test-Path proving nothing was created, and 4/4 junction-evasion cases refused. The historical parents[2] dead-code condition is genuinely fixed (parents[3] verified at runtime, and the refusals demonstrably fire). (6) 'Cannot write production' is proven empirically, not just by reading code: with a sys.addaudithook tripwire raising on any write/mkdir/remove/rename/subprocess/socket under the three repos, the production .source_catalog or the real root, a full build and a full probe both completed with blocked_count=0 and production_catalog_open_count=0, and every observed write landed in %TEMP%. (7) The production catalog metadata matches the record exactly at my two earlier stats; a -shm movement I observed at 21:00:15Z was outside the reviewed window, unattributable, and followed by a flat 25 s baseline - which independently validates the report's G5 non-attribution wording. (8) The directive does not promote any 2026-09-13 unauthorized item, and the actions really were read-only. The report also does not claim B08 passed and explicitly forbids that reading. It is nevertheless not APPROVE: there are two substantive overclaims about what was verified - the tamper case is described as a real-content divergence test when it only trips the handle version-pin gate before any file access (B-VR08L2-01, P2), and the real-directory zero-side-effect snapshot covers only the direct files of one directory while the report states it as a general per-file before/after (B-VR08L2-02, P2) - plus four P3s (self-asserted read-only literals; an absolute 'no new files in the repository' that is literally refuted by a gitignored .pyc; an inconsistent L12 grade; an imprecise isolated-write path) and one out-of-scope directive naming/supersession note. None of these invalidates the level-2 result; all are wording-or-coverage issues that a one-pass revision of the report and one added case can close.
not_checked: OS-level process observation (which process opened which file, via Win32/NT handles): not obtainable on this host without extra tooling. My substitute is an IN-PROCESS Python audit hook, so it observes only this process's Python-level API calls; a C extension, an open performed outside the audited calls, or any OTHER process on the machine would not be seen. The report registers this same half as unobtainable and I agree.

Production catalog CONTENT: forbidden by my instructions and by the directive, so 'unchanged' is a metadata-only statement (size + mtime). A content write that preserved both size and mtime would be invisible to me and to the tools. I consider this the residual risk of the whole zero-side-effect claim, and it is inherent to the authorization, not a defect of the work.

Writer-boundary cases: write-mode occupation, concurrent replacement (TOCTOU with a real writer), real ACLs, cloud placeholders and symlink escape - all need either write access to production bytes or an environment I must not create. The report declines to claim them; I did not test them.

L03 / L07 / L10's real-corpus halves (real move/rename, real revision pairs, real sections artifacts) - out of reach for the same reasons; for L10 I verified only the A05-5/A05-5b count the report cites (85 ids, 0 sections).

I did not re-run evidence/b08_level2_run.py against the reviewed isolated root, deliberately: that would have mutated the artifact under review. I built into my own temp root (%TEMP%\b08l2-reviewer\iso-audit) instead and got identical counts, so 'the reviewed isolated database is exactly what the recorded build produced' is inferred from count/entity/last_scanned_at equality plus a byte-identical probe re-run against it, not from a byte-for-byte re-build in place.

My three probe re-runs did open the reviewed isolated catalog (the probe itself connects to it read-write), which removed its transient -wal/-shm on clean close; I verified the contents are unchanged, but I did not preserve the pre-review byte image of that temp artifact.

The A05 command manifest, the excluded command list and all B.AR/B09 artifacts: not audited (a different work package). Finding B-VR08L2-07 is a naming/status observation from the directive's cross-reference only.
filing-fetch: nothing in it participates in level 2; I verified only its HEAD and the guard's refusal coverage of its path.
_real_root_state's cap=200 truncation was reasoned from code, not exercised (the real root has 2 files; my mutation experiment used 3). Its behaviour with a >200-file real root is therefore untested.

The report's claim that the superseded vacuous probe versions existed and produced MISSING / 0 matches (F1): the superseded code is gone, so I could confirm only the mechanism (the entity gate would indeed match nothing for a fabricated or Unresolved entity) and that the current probe anchors a real identity - not the historical runs.
Whether the choice function's tie-break among the eight equally small candidate directories matters for G7 representativeness: I checked only that the chosen directory satisfies the stated criterion.
